newsitem.title: USA: Lead treatment charges seen rising in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Lead treatment charges seen rising in 1997.

text.p: Lead treatment charges may well rise for 1997 contracts despite some miners looking for terms unchanged from last year, industry officials said on Monday.

"Lead seems to be coming out about like last year," David Thompson, president and chief executive of Cominco Ltd, told Reuters. "I don't think there is going to be any big change. There has been one settlement."
In 1996 the miners and smelters settled on a benchmark price of about $175 per tonne with a base London Metal Exchange lead cash price of $600 per tonne.
Many lead industry officials are in Scottsdale to attend the American Zinc Association's annual meeting, traditionally an event where lead and zinc benchmark prices are hammered out.

"There is almost an endemic surplus (of lead concentrates), and it will probably get worse in the next few years with the Cannington mine," Thompson said. He was referring to The Broken Hill's new mine in Australia's Queensland state.
Canada's Cominco Ltd is a significant miner and smelter of lead and zinc.
Smelters are able to push up what they charge mines to treat concentrates if availability of material is plentiful. In a tight market, miners can push down prices as smelters scramble for feed.
But other lead mining officials attending the conference admitted it would be difficult to stop the smelters from obtaining higher treatment charges.
"It is difficult to say that the market is tight," one European lead miner said. He expects lead treatment charges to rise by a few dollars.
A lead concentrates buyer at a European smelter was offered unchanged treatment charges by a North American miner for 1997. "But we are asking for at least $10 higher this year," the buyer said.
Lead smelter officials said the one unknown in the concentrates picture is exactly when Anvil Range Mining's Faro lead and zinc mine in Canada's Yukon would come back on stream.
Faro, shut down on December 20, is a significant producer of lead concentrates, and many delegates here expect it to come back on stream before the end of ther year.
